correctness.rationale: Tilted two-state Feynman–Kac reduction is explicit; the positive real part of b times conjugate z excludes all nonzero-asymmetry coherence zeros, and symmetric zeros are enumerated. The squared-modulus derivative is a strictly convex envelope subtracted from a cosine. Positivity sets have at most one component in each positive cosine lobe. The uniform scaled-envelope limit and two-sided lobe-count sandwich prove the asymptotic coefficient. The local zero rounding follows from implicit-function and analytic parity. Direct independent numerical propagation corroborates, but does not replace, these proofs.
